what_happened: The job to refuse oversized multi-surface readings before dispatch (a `check_job_size` rule) was rejected at the final verdict. One of 6 acceptance criteria was unmet: the test that `check_job_size` refuses readings shaped like job t67q and job zaj2. There were two blocker findings and three major ones. The first blocker: the real zaj2 reading spans 3 groups and 11 deliverables, so the check accepts it and one of the two target failures is not prevented. The second blocker: the zaj2 test fixture was invented and does not match the job's recorded deliverables. The majors: a doc comment makes a false claim about zaj2; the group bound is too coarse, because all code counts as one group and only a reading spanning all four groups is refused, and the 30-deliverable backstop is far above both failed jobs (9 and 11); and the accepted reading did not match the request. No checks are listed as failed.
cause: The reading cited past jobs by id but nothing resolved those ids to their recorded deliverables before the reading was accepted. The thresholds (3 groups, 30 deliverables) and the test fixture were then built from an assumed shape. Nothing required the new rule to run against the real records of the jobs it names, and the criteria checked that the fixtures were refused, not that the real jobs would be. A check that passes only on its own invented input proves nothing. This is close to the earlier reading/provenance mismatch cases, but the distinct gap is a threshold and fixture never replayed against recorded failures. The same replay idea already exists for refusal rules over past requests; it was not applied to this size rule.
prevention: When a request or reading adds a refusal rule that cites past jobs, Athena should resolve each cited job id to its recorded reading and deliverables at reading time. The criteria should then require the rule's test to load those recorded shapes, not invented fixtures. The rule's thresholds should be set from the measured sizes of the cited failed jobs and of landed jobs, so the rule demonstrably refuses the failures and accepts the successes. A code check should fail any fixture labelled with a job id that differs from that job's recorded data.
proposed_request: Make `check_job_size` refuse oversized multi-surface readings before dispatch, using recorded data only. (1) Read the recorded readings and deliverables of jobs 20261025-183644-t67q and 20261017-205554-zaj2 from the records, and state their real group and deliverable counts. (2) Replace the invented ZAJ2_SHAPE fixture and the corpus entry with fixtures loaded from those recorded shapes, and correct the doc comment so it states only what the records show. (3) Set the group and deliverable bounds from those measured counts and from the counts of recently landed jobs, so that both failed jobs are refused and the landed jobs are accepted. Count code across crates, tests and xtask as separate surfaces if that is what separates the failed jobs from the landed ones. (4) The refusal message must say to split the job by surface and dependency. (5) Add a test in `cargo test -p athena-core` that runs the check on both recorded shapes and on a set of landed job shapes. It must fail when the `step!` line is removed. (6) Add a CHANGELOG.md entry.
